ERMELO PONZI SCHEME

By: Este de Klerk | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
When someone you trust offers you the opportunity to invest money and receive an extraordinary monthly return on your investment, why would you let the opportunity slip?

Unique Selling Point:
When someone you trust offers you the opportunity to invest money and receive an extraordinary monthly return on your investment, why would you let the opportunity slip?
More than 1300 investors countrywide, with almost half of them based in the small Mpumalanga town of Ermelo, invested a total of R282 million in two years in a company called "Love and Let's Live" belonging to Ermelo resident, Andre Willem Theron, who renamed himself A'ri'El Willem Theron.
Theron promised an 8% monthly return on investment - and as a ponzi scheme works, delivered that to earlier investors promptly.
The deal was to trade the money in foreign currencies.
It was a scheme of epic proportions.
Theron - in letters to investors and the attorney working with the liquidators - denied ever running a ponzi scheme, ever planning a scheme, but "innocently" wrote several letters to investors when the bomb burst apologising for the loss of their money, said he was "very sorry", "would give his life to them, but unfortunately had to leave the country to start a new life and was now making a nomadic existence in South America".
Investors have opened five separate criminal cases with the SAPS, but nothing has come of it...
Love and Let's Live has finally been liquidated in July 2018 and Theron has been sequestrated.
R15 million has flowed to his close family members.
R6 million salaries were paid out in two years.
Theron falsified a Forex Trading account statement which he showed to investors in December 2017, that stated there was USD110 million in the account, when in fact there was only USD353 in the account.
The forensic audit states that only 1,5% of the total amount invested was in fact traded on foreign currencies and this was done at a loss.
So what happened to all the money?

Summary:
-An application to liquidate - or wind-up - Love and Let's Live Pty (Ltd), the company belonging to A'riel Willem Theron - a 30-year old resident from Ermelo who operated a so-called "Ponzi scheme" with 1 356 investors' money - was brought by creditors as an urgent application in the Pretoria High Court on 6 December 2017

-A provisional liquidation order was issued by the Pretoria High Court on 30 January 2018

-A Final liquidation order was issued on 16 March 2018

-The effective date of the liquidation of LLL was on 6 December 2017 - the date on which the urgent application was heard by the Pretoria High Court

-On 6 February 2018, Hannes Muller and Lariska Arends from the Tshwane Trust in Pretoria were appointed as the provisional liquidators of LLL

-Muller and Arends immediately started to act according to the insolvency legislation - seizing assets and financial records of LLL. They also approached the High Court to ask for permission to start formal and official questioning of related individuals

-The liquidators don't know what the current whereabouts of Theron are - he earlier informed them via email that he is "now living a wanderer's lifestyle in South America", and he refused to provide the liquidators with any information to assist them with their investigation

-The financial records were investigated and forensic report was written containing information about how money flowed in the company

-1 357 Investors paid over a total amount of R290 390 780 to LLL

-According to a written agreement between investors and LLL, a return in investment of between 72 and 96% would have been derived from trade in foreign currency

-From the financial records, it seems that only 5,12% of investors' money LLL received was in fact used to trade in foreign currency AND these investments were traded against a loss




Further information:
-The return in investment (monies) paid out to investors by far superseded the identifiable sources of income and the excessive returns paid out to certain investors were paid from funds received from other investors = Ponzi scheme -From the forensic report, it seems that LLL's liabilities exceeded its assets - possibly already as early as two months after LLL started to do business with investors
-A further complication was that some investors didn't pay over their investment monies to the bank accounts of LLL, but to Theron's personal bank account and some specifically paid it over to a bank account Theron holds in Mauritius

-The liquidators were able to determine that no money remained in the Mauritius account when LLL was liquidated - but they need to obtain a court order in Mauritius - a lengthy and costly exercise - in order to have access to bank statements of that account

-An amount of at least R15 352 326 (R15 million) was siphoned from LLL's bank accounts to close family relatives of Theron, LLL director. A further amount of R8 million (R8 388 138) was given to Theron's sister with which she bought a property in Cape Town. The liquidators have already started the process to seize money and assets that were unlawfully siphoned to Theron's family members

-R51-million (R51 743 200) of the money received by LLL was used to purchase a farm just outside Ermelo in the name of a company called "Ruby Success Inv - an entity of which Theron's father, Andre Theron was a director. The liquidators managed to have Ruby Success liquidated and Willem Theron sequestrated - declared insolvent

-Provisional curators were appointed in the insolvent estate of Theron and they're currently in the process of selling the assets contained in the estate - two properties in Pretoria of which he is a 50% owner, furniture and three vehicles - it is not plausible that excessive funds would be obtained from selling his personal assets: the vehicles are still under financing and the properties still under mortgage.

-The assets in Ruby Success - the farm - was sold on auction for R22-million (R22 200 000), so at a loss of R29-million of the price Theron paid when he bought it.

-The liquidators have received claims from 450 creditors for a total amount of R170-million (R170 085 843,56). The liquidators are investigating the amounts claimed from creditors, as it seems that creditors have not only claimed the money they invested with LLL, but also the astronomical return on investment they were promised

-According to Insolvency Legislation - also used in court cases such as the infamous Krion case - the aim is to fairly divide the return on assets amongst creditors - obtained from liquidated entities - the legislation makes provision that - for the time period before the entity was liquidated -- transactions that took place in favor of certain investors in comparison with other investors who were not advantaged - should be set aside = this means that the astronomical return in investments that investors received are now being seized to claim back money that would then later fairly be distributed between all the creditors

-After the provisional liquidation date of LLL on 6 December 2017, LLL paid back certain investors' monies. According to article 341 (2) of the Companies' Act, such payments are regarded as null and void and those monies have to be seized by the liquidators

-LLL also started to pay back investors' money shortly before the liquidation on 6 December - it seems that the aim was to pay back investors who'd put in less money, first at the expense of investors who invested large sums of money. The liquidators are also currently seizing any money paid back to investors within a six month period before LLL was liquidated (in terms of to Article 29 of the Insolvency Act).

-According to the liquidators it is CLEAR that LLL was run as an illegal scheme and therefore all the exorbitant amounts of interest on their return on investments paid to investors, were done unlawfully and illegally. In terms of the Insolvency Act (article 26) all the interest received by investors have to be paid back as what is termed "disposals without value".

-As soon as the liquidators have finished the process, the available funds would be divided on a pro rata base to creditors - this could still take months due to certain court actions that need to take place

-Up until this stage, a total amount of R5,78 million (R5 798 616,23) has been seized by the liquidators.

INFORMATION GATHERED FROM THE FORENSIC REPORT (NOT TO BE QUOTED DIRECTLY)

DEFINITIONS OF A PONZI SCHEME:

THE USA'S SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION DEFINITION:
"A Ponzi scheme is an investment fraud that involves the payment of purported returns ro existing investors from funds contributed by new investors. Ponzi scheme organisers often solicit new investors by promising to invest funds in opportunities claimed to generate high returns with little or no risk. In many Ponzi schemes, the fraudsters focus on attracting new money to make promised payments to earlier-stage investors to create false appearance that investors are profiting from a legitimate business."

THE SOUTH AFRICAN RESERVE BANK DEFINITION:
"Names after the person - Charles Ponzi - who first made these schemes infamous, they are operated by tricksters and sometimes seemingly legitimate businesses that will invite you to invest in a scheme or business. The operator promises you unrealistically large returns on your investment in a short period of time.

These schemes depend on enticing a steady flow of investors, whose money goes to pay off promises made to earlier investors. Any such scheme will inevitably collapse, as it is impossible to find enough investors to keep the scheme going."

PONZI SCHEMES SHARE CERTAIN COMMON CHARACTERISTICS (A LAWYER MUST EXPLAIN THIS)

"The purported business underlying the investment scheme depends on the inflow of external investor money;
"The investor money is not used according to the stated business purpose. Instead, the investor money is used to pay returns to earlier investors, to often fund the perpetrator's lifestyle, or for some other illegitimate prupose;
"The purported business enterprise underlying the scheme lacks sufficient profit to provide the returns and, therefore, depends on a continually increasing inflow of new investor money, and
"Ponzi schemes often involve a charismatic and confident central promoter who successfully swindles investors

SABRICS'S WARNING SIGNS OF A PONZI SCHEME:

"The promoter promises high returns, which could not be achieved through normal conventional investment opportunities, within a short period.
"In some cases, the promoter will use fake qualifications or references to entice investors, for example, an "attorney with many years' experience in the stock market"
"Often high returns are paid initially, and then investors are lured into investing even more money
"They often promise guaranteed returns - no return is ever guaranteed, all investments carry some risk
"Promoters are usually quite secretive about the actual business model
"The promoter becomes unavailable and returns dry up
"Usually, the scheme collapses soon after that

FSB ISSUED A WARNING ABOUT ADNRE WILLEM THERON:

The attorney, Krog, informed the forensic auditors firm who conducted the forensic analysis that they have determined during their interviews that the Financial Services Board (FSB) investigated LLL during may 2017 and referred the matter to the south African Reserve Bank.
The FSB issued a notification that AW Theron is not registered as a financial services provider in terms of the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002.

MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN LLL AND INVESTORS:

According to the MOU signed between the LLL and investors:

"Funds will be placed in an accredited online trading account, and trading will take place on an accredited trading platform, of which account trader (A'riel Willem Theron [ID: 880917 5149 083]) and EA's (Expert Advisors) will be the predominant trading tools, trading a variety of Forex currencies. The agreement is that all deposited funds will grow at a monthly rate of 8%, cumulative."


LLL'S BANK ACCOUNTS FROZEN AND CLOSED:

"One company that appeared to have been a forex trader was identified
"FNB froze LLL's accounts in mid 2017
"During the latter part of 2017, FNB closed LLL's bank accounts
"Krog explained that two employees then agreed to set-up a company called Lemon Tree Admin (Pty) Ltd - They opened a Standard Bank account in the name if Lemon Tree. LLL transferred funds to Lemon Tree's account to mostly make further payments to investors

AW THERON'S EXPLANATION AS TO WHAT HAPPENED TO MONEY:

The liquidator stated that when investors brought the liquidation application in December 2017, Theron responded that: "THE FUNDS WERE INVESTED IN BITCOIN BUT THEN STOLEN BY HACKERS". Moreover, "THAT ALL THE FUNDS ARE GONE".

THERON LEAVING SA:

Krog confirmed that AW Theron left South Africa for Brazil on 17 January 2018.
The Ermelo Magistrate's Court issues a warrant for his arrest after investors in Ermelo laif a complaint with the SAPS.

THERON ALLEGEDLY FALSIFIED LLL'S AVATRADER ACCOUNT AND BALANCE INFORMATION:

"From information provided by Krog, it seems that AW Theron showed protential investors an AvaTrader account statement that indicated the balance as USD110 923 462.90 (110 million US dollars) on 31 December 2017.
"In an email, on 19 March 2018 mr Ian Webb from AvaTrader, however, stated that: "I can confirm that the attached is not a true document. It is a screenshot from Ava Metatrader login page but the details have been altered."
"The correct balance was confirmed to be USD353

Press Release:


Ermelo Investment Horror
It’s been ten months since the R290 million crypto-currency investment scheme Love and Let’s Live initially operating from Ermelo, Mpumalanga, collapsed, leaving more than 1300 investors, including pensioners and local business owners in a deep financial crisis. Trading on neighbourly trust and lifetime acquaintances, the company owner promised investors 8% monthly returns which were initially promptly paid out, attracting even more investors. Now the forex trader has fled the country. Carte Blanche uncovers how the scheme collapsed – leaving hundreds of devastated investors behind.
Producer: Esté de Klerk
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


ERMELO PONZI SCHEME

PRODUCER: ESTE DE KLERK
PRESENTER: MACFARLANE MOLELI
EDITOR: STENETTE GROSKOPF
BROADCAST DATE: 11 NOVEMBER 2018

When Meyerton resident William Holliday's father, Alfred passed away in November 2016, he had only one wish: that 34-year old William should take care of his stepmom, Phoebe and his two younger brothers.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Hy het my aanhoudend gevra, veral die laaste rukkie, "Asseblief kyk na jou broers. Kyk na die geld. Maak seker dit is vasbelê.
(He asked me continuously, especially towards the end, "Please look after your brothers. Look after the money. Make sure that it's invested.")

Financially, William's dad provided well for the family and it was only a matter of where to invest the money to secure their future.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Ons het 'n belegging gesoek om 'n manier om die geldjies te bele sodat ons kan vir die kinders se kollege, as hulle kollege wil gaan - eerste karretjie, sulke goedjies.
(We were looking for an investment, a way to invest the money for the children's future college education, would they want to go to college… for their first cars, things like that.)

A'ri'El Willem Theron immediately came to mind. William met Theron years ago and remembered him speaking about his business - investing people's money with above average return on investments.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Hy was redelik baie wetend, baie intelligent, so ek het nogal geglo hy maak die geld. Ek het nogal geval vir dit.
(He was relatively knowledgeable, very intelligent… So, I believed he made the money. I fell for it.)

PHOEBE HOLLIDAY: So het ek my geld toe in Januarie 2017 daar bele. En ek dink my eerste payout wat ek gekry het was in Maart. Ek het vir die kinders gesê daardie jaar ek gaan sabbatical vat.
(So, I invested my money there in January 2017. And I think I received my first pay-out in March. I told the children that I was going to take a sabbatical that year.)

Thirty-year old Willem Theron, originally from Ermelo in Mpumalanga, was described by many as a financial whizz kid - trading in a variety of foreign currency.
Through his company - Love and Let's Live - he changed the financial prospects of his investors: an 8% monthly growth on investments.

LINK: About 600 people from the town of Ermelo invested their money in Love and Let's Live and the town was abuzz with the new found wealth. However, it all came crashing down in January 2018.

In just two years, more than 1300 people invested R290 million.
The Love and Let's Live business model was based on what the South African Reserve Bank describes as a typical pyramid scheme: as long as new investors poured in money, the agreed 8% return on investment could be paid out to earlier-stage investors.

HANNES MULLER: There was, however, no underlying business or trading.

Liquidator, Hanner Muller - who handled Love and Let's Live's liquidation after the scheme collapsed - says forensic statements show that, contrary to Willem's written agreement with investors, only a fraction of the money was in fact traded in foreign currency.

HANNES MULLER: only about five percent of what he ever collected was used for trading and that was done at a loss.

Mathys Krog is an attorney assisting Hannes and his team in trying to recover some of the money.

MATHYS KROG: He generated an Excel spreadsheet. People think, "I've invested R100 000. Now I've got R180 000 after three or four months." They will think that is the money they have in that account. Unfortunately, that was only a book entry. There was no such thing.

Andre van Staden has been a restaurant owner in Ermelo for almost two decades.

ANDRE VAN STADEN/RESTAURANT OWNER: If somebody comes to you in a community like this..." because we know everyone "... and shows you the papers and tell you, 'Andre, for the last 6 years I've been making R60,000 a month, I would believe them immediately.

VO: Willem was a prefect at the Ermelo Christian School.

LINK: Those who knew and grew up with him, described him as a humble, Christian boy who was loved and trusted by the community.

ATHOL STARK: This was somebody that we knew. This was a personal family friend.

Athol Stark is an astute businessman in Ermelo. He and two of his sons invested fairly large amounts.

ATHOL STARK: What we definitely saw was that people's lifestyles had improved dramatically in the town. It was based on their success that other people started to jump on board.

ANDRE VAN STADEN:People went to banks and borrowed money to put into this scheme. Many people took second mortgages on their homes.

Ermelo residents were lining up - and like Theron's father, Andre - well-known in town - believed in the man who made it all happen.
Andre Theron and his wife left town and moved to Makhado, but he agreed to speak to us telephonically.

ANDRE THERON: He was trading successfully and that I still believe. It was never a big business from day one, it was just a small thing that grew.

With Love and Let's Live offering a 2% "referral incentive ", friends informed friends and soon business was booming - for Willem Theron and his investors.

ANDRE THERON: Willem never ever asked anybody to invest in his business, never. So, he got people asking him if they could invest and he always told them exactly that it is high risk, he is doing well.

In April last year, R41 million flowed from Love and Let's Live's bank accounts as a cash deposit for the ultimate gift from son to father: a 3000 hectare luxury game and apple farm nestled in the lush green hills of the Mpumalanga highveld. The Therons had big plans, stocking the farm with valuable game and transforming an old shed to extravagant hunter's lodgings.
Gerhard Serfontein was the building contractor.

MACFARLANE MOLELI: What did it cost to build this place?

GERHARD SERFONTEIN: It cost approximately 3 point something million. This was built especially for hunters coming from America and Spain and all over.

Not only did Willem's dad profit.
A forensic report indicates that R15,3 million was disbursed to Willem and his closest family members.
More than R6 million was siphoned to Willem himself.

MACFARLANE: Did you get up to R15 million, and your family, from your son, Willem?

ANDRE THERON: I SPENT EVERYTHING ON THE FARM. The money was used for the farm, it went through my account, but I didn't use it for myself.

According to the report, of the R290 million invested, R196 million was paid back to investors between 2015 and 2017.

Theron, however, was trading illegally.

MACFARLANE: Did he have an FSB licence?

ANDRE THERON: No, of course what he did was illegal - and I know that he was trying to get it legalised.

It seemed that Theron was caught off-guard when the Financial Services Board issued a warning to the public in July last year not to invest with Love and Let's Live as the company was not an authorised Financial Services Provider.
Shortly after this, the bank froze the company accounts.

Between August 2017 and January this year, Willem Theron wrote a series of letters to investors - promising full refunds to them all.

PHOEBE HOLLIDAY: Daardie September toe my huur moes betaal toe is daar net nie die fondse nie.
(That September, when I had to pay my rent, there were no funds available.)

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: My stiefma het goed uit haar huis begin verkoop om net vanaf te lewe.
My stepmom started to sell things in her house in order to be able to survive.

Willem Theron did not respond to our questions, but in a leaked telephone conversation with investors earlier this year, he explained he drained his international trading account worth over a hundred million dollars - and poured all the money into buying Bitcoin at 8000 dollars per unit.

[MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: Die bitcoin wat ons gekoop het, was meer as 14 000 bitcoin.
(The Bitcoin that we bought was more than 14 000 Bitcoin.)

But the forensic auditors couldn't find any Bitcoin ledger transactions that proved this.

MATHYS KROG: We did find a Bitcoin wallet. There were at one stage 213 or 217 Bitcoins.we traced about 157 of those Bitcoins.

In correspondence to investors, Theron stated that Love and Let's Live was not a ponzi scheme.
He insisted that he had more than double what was owed to clients and that the majority of the money in the international trading account was his.

[MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: DIE Klientegeld wat in die rekening was was 50 million dollar en die res van die geld was myne.
The clients' money that was in the account was 50 million dollar and the rest of the money was mine.

In early January, he announced he was closing the business and all outstanding investments would be refunded.
However, two weeks later, he claimed the Bitcoin he "had in storage for the remainder of the payments was stolen through a sophisticated and ruthless hacking operation".
He fled the country and said he hoped investors would one day be able to forgive him.

MACFARLANE: WHERE IS YOUR SON AT THE MOMENT?

VOICE OF ANDRE THERON: HE IS SOMEWHERE IN SOUTH AMERICA

MACFARLANE: Why did he run away, why isn't he coming to face the music?

VOICE OF ANDRE THERON: The question is this: are you ready to ask your son to come back and let him go to a South African jail?

[MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: Ek gaan nie lieg as ek se ek is nogsteeds baie dankbaar dat ek nie raakgesien word op hierdie oomblik nie, ek is baie skaam daaroor. Ek is ook baie jammer vir alles wat tot dusver gebeur het.
(I'm not going to lie when I say I am still very thankful that I am not being seen at this moment - I feel very ashamed. I am also very sorry for what has happened thus far.)

VOICE OF ANDRE VAN STADEN: When all the news came through, that 2 months were terrible for us because we could see people were spending less money.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Nie net dat ons almal gedependant aan die geld wat gaan uit gaan betaal word nie, so al die skuld wat ons gemaak het sou gecover gewees het. vir my ook omdat ek alles verloor het, maar meer vir my stiefma omdat dit my boeties se toekoms is.

Not only were we all dependent on the money that was going to be paid out because all the debt we entered into would have been covered by that. The realisation that everything is gone, is a lot for me to handle. Obviously, also for myself because I have lost everything, but more so for my stepmom because it's my brothers' future… It would have secured her future.

ATHOL STARK: "How could he do this to us?" This was somebody that we actually trusted.

To make matters worse, every cent that investors RECEIVED in interest on their initial investments, they now have to pay back to the liquidators as stipulated by the Insolvency Act.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Ek moet 120 duisend terug betaal. My stiefma moet 200 duisend terug betaal. Ons het nie daardie geld nie.
I have to pay back R120 000. My stepmom has to pay back R200 000. We don't have that kind of money.

The farm was liquidated and sold on auction and like so many other investors, Andre Theron says he also lost everything.

ANDRE THERON: A LOT OF PEOPLE LOST EVERYTHING, I AM ONE OF THEM, I AM TRYING TO BUILD A NEW LIFE

A total of eight fraud cases have been opened against Willem Theron and the police has issued a warrant for his arrest.
To date, the liquidators have only been able to recover R7 million. Many investors will never see their money again.

ATHOL STARK: Hundreds of people in this town are in severe financial crisis. They've lost their homes. They've lost their vehicles. They've lost their pensions based on what have happened with Willem Theron and his scheme.

******

PROMOS

PROMO 1: 30"
Would you invest money when someone you trust offers you a lifetime-opportunity to earn higher-than-bank returns?

ANDRE VAN STADEN: People went to banks and borrowed money to put into this scheme. Many people took second mortgages on their homes.

More than a thousand people invested R290 million in a scheme initially run from Ermelo, Mpumalanga and are reeling from shock after the scheme's collapse.

WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: My stiefma het goed uit haar huis begin verkoop om net vanaf te lewe.

PROMO 2: 15"

A financial whizz kid from Ermelo in Mpumalanga dramatically changed the lives of more than a thousand people who invested millions with his company. But then the scheme collapsed and the whizz kid fled the country.

ATHOL STARK: How could he do this to us, cause this is someone that we actually trusted?

PROMO 3: 15"
More than 600 residents of Ermelo in Mpumalanga invested millions with a local financial "whizz kid" they all trusted.

ATHOL STARK: people's lifestyles had improved dramatically in the town.

Until the scheme collapsed… and they lost everything. Residents in town now reeling with shock.

PROMO 4: 10"

With an 8% monthly return on investment promised, a man from Ermelo, Mpumalanga took over a thousand investors for a ride that's left many destitute and a whole town in shock.

Unique Selling Point: When someone you trust offers you the opportunity to invest money and receive an extraordinary monthly return on your investment, why would you let the opportunity slip? More than 1300 investors countrywide, with almost half of them based in the small Mpumalanga town of Ermelo, invested a total of R282 million in two years in a company called "Love and Let's Live" belonging to Ermelo resident, Andre Willem Theron, who renamed himself A'ri'El Willem Theron. Theron promised an 8% monthly return on investment - and as a ponzi scheme works, delivered that to earlier investors promptly. The deal was to trade the money in foreign currencies. It was a scheme of epic proportions. Theron - in letters to investors and the attorney working with the liquidators - denied ever running a ponzi scheme, ever planning a scheme, but "innocently" wrote several letters to investors when the bomb burst apologising for the loss of their money, said he was "very sorry", "would give his life to them, but unfortunately had to leave the country to start a new life and was now making a nomadic existence in South America". Investors have opened five separate criminal cases with the SAPS, but nothing has come of it... Love and Let's Live has finally been liquidated in July 2018 and Theron has been sequestrated. R15 million has flowed to his close family members. R6 million salaries were paid out in two years. Theron falsified a Forex Trading account statement which he showed to investors in December 2017, that stated there was USD110 million in the account, when in fact there was only USD353 in the account. The forensic audit states that only 1,5% of the total amount invested was in fact traded on foreign currencies and this was done at a loss. So what happened to all the money? Summary: -An application to liquidate - or wind-up - Love and Let's Live Pty (Ltd), the company belonging to A'riel Willem Theron - a 30-year old resident from Ermelo who operated a so-called "Ponzi scheme" with 1 356 investors' money - was brought by creditors as an urgent application in the Pretoria High Court on 6 December 2017 -A provisional liquidation order was issued by the Pretoria High Court on 30 January 2018 -A Final liquidation order was issued on 16 March 2018 -The effective date of the liquidation of LLL was on 6 December 2017 - the date on which the urgent application was heard by the Pretoria High Court -On 6 February 2018, Hannes Muller and Lariska Arends from the Tshwane Trust in Pretoria were appointed as the provisional liquidators of LLL -Muller and Arends immediately started to act according to the insolvency legislation - seizing assets and financial records of LLL. They also approached the High Court to ask for permission to start formal and official questioning of related individuals -The liquidators don't know what the current whereabouts of Theron are - he earlier informed them via email that he is "now living a wanderer's lifestyle in South America", and he refused to provide the liquidators with any information to assist them with their investigation -The financial records were investigated and forensic report was written containing information about how money flowed in the company -1 357 Investors paid over a total amount of R290 390 780 to LLL -According to a written agreement between investors and LLL, a return in investment of between 72 and 96% would have been derived from trade in foreign currency -From the financial records, it seems that only 5,12% of investors' money LLL received was in fact used to trade in foreign currency AND these investments were traded against a loss Further information: -The return in investment (monies) paid out to investors by far superseded the identifiable sources of income and the excessive returns paid out to certain investors were paid from funds received from other investors = Ponzi scheme -From the forensic report, it seems that LLL's liabilities exceeded its assets - possibly already as early as two months after LLL started to do business with investors -A further complication was that some investors didn't pay over their investment monies to the bank accounts of LLL, but to Theron's personal bank account and some specifically paid it over to a bank account Theron holds in Mauritius -The liquidators were able to determine that no money remained in the Mauritius account when LLL was liquidated - but they need to obtain a court order in Mauritius - a lengthy and costly exercise - in order to have access to bank statements of that account -An amount of at least R15 352 326 (R15 million) was siphoned from LLL's bank accounts to close family relatives of Theron, LLL director. A further amount of R8 million (R8 388 138) was given to Theron's sister with which she bought a property in Cape Town. The liquidators have already started the process to seize money and assets that were unlawfully siphoned to Theron's family members -R51-million (R51 743 200) of the money received by LLL was used to purchase a farm just outside Ermelo in the name of a company called "Ruby Success Inv - an entity of which Theron's father, Andre Theron was a director. The liquidators managed to have Ruby Success liquidated and Willem Theron sequestrated - declared insolvent -Provisional curators were appointed in the insolvent estate of Theron and they're currently in the process of selling the assets contained in the estate - two properties in Pretoria of which he is a 50% owner, furniture and three vehicles - it is not plausible that excessive funds would be obtained from selling his personal assets: the vehicles are still under financing and the properties still under mortgage. -The assets in Ruby Success - the farm - was sold on auction for R22-million (R22 200 000), so at a loss of R29-million of the price Theron paid when he bought it. -The liquidators have received claims from 450 creditors for a total amount of R170-million (R170 085 843,56). The liquidators are investigating the amounts claimed from creditors, as it seems that creditors have not only claimed the money they invested with LLL, but also the astronomical return on investment they were promised -According to Insolvency Legislation - also used in court cases such as the infamous Krion case - the aim is to fairly divide the return on assets amongst creditors - obtained from liquidated entities - the legislation makes provision that - for the time period before the entity was liquidated -- transactions that took place in favor of certain investors in comparison with other investors who were not advantaged - should be set aside = this means that the astronomical return in investments that investors received are now being seized to claim back money that would then later fairly be distributed between all the creditors -After the provisional liquidation date of LLL on 6 December 2017, LLL paid back certain investors' monies. According to article 341 (2) of the Companies' Act, such payments are regarded as null and void and those monies have to be seized by the liquidators -LLL also started to pay back investors' money shortly before the liquidation on 6 December - it seems that the aim was to pay back investors who'd put in less money, first at the expense of investors who invested large sums of money. The liquidators are also currently seizing any money paid back to investors within a six month period before LLL was liquidated (in terms of to Article 29 of the Insolvency Act). -According to the liquidators it is CLEAR that LLL was run as an illegal scheme and therefore all the exorbitant amounts of interest on their return on investments paid to investors, were done unlawfully and illegally. In terms of the Insolvency Act (article 26) all the interest received by investors have to be paid back as what is termed "disposals without value". -As soon as the liquidators have finished the process, the available funds would be divided on a pro rata base to creditors - this could still take months due to certain court actions that need to take place -Up until this stage, a total amount of R5,78 million (R5 798 616,23) has been seized by the liquidators. INFORMATION GATHERED FROM THE FORENSIC REPORT (NOT TO BE QUOTED DIRECTLY) DEFINITIONS OF A PONZI SCHEME: THE USA'S SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION DEFINITION: "A Ponzi scheme is an investment fraud that involves the payment of purported returns ro existing investors from funds contributed by new investors. Ponzi scheme organisers often solicit new investors by promising to invest funds in opportunities claimed to generate high returns with little or no risk. In many Ponzi schemes, the fraudsters focus on attracting new money to make promised payments to earlier-stage investors to create false appearance that investors are profiting from a legitimate business." THE SOUTH AFRICAN RESERVE BANK DEFINITION: "Names after the person - Charles Ponzi - who first made these schemes infamous, they are operated by tricksters and sometimes seemingly legitimate businesses that will invite you to invest in a scheme or business. The operator promises you unrealistically large returns on your investment in a short period of time. These schemes depend on enticing a steady flow of investors, whose money goes to pay off promises made to earlier investors. Any such scheme will inevitably collapse, as it is impossible to find enough investors to keep the scheme going." PONZI SCHEMES SHARE CERTAIN COMMON CHARACTERISTICS (A LAWYER MUST EXPLAIN THIS) "The purported business underlying the investment scheme depends on the inflow of external investor money; "The investor money is not used according to the stated business purpose. Instead, the investor money is used to pay returns to earlier investors, to often fund the perpetrator's lifestyle, or for some other illegitimate prupose; "The purported business enterprise underlying the scheme lacks sufficient profit to provide the returns and, therefore, depends on a continually increasing inflow of new investor money, and "Ponzi schemes often involve a charismatic and confident central promoter who successfully swindles investors SABRICS'S WARNING SIGNS OF A PONZI SCHEME: "The promoter promises high returns, which could not be achieved through normal conventional investment opportunities, within a short period. "In some cases, the promoter will use fake qualifications or references to entice investors, for example, an "attorney with many years' experience in the stock market" "Often high returns are paid initially, and then investors are lured into investing even more money "They often promise guaranteed returns - no return is ever guaranteed, all investments carry some risk "Promoters are usually quite secretive about the actual business model "The promoter becomes unavailable and returns dry up "Usually, the scheme collapses soon after that FSB ISSUED A WARNING ABOUT ADNRE WILLEM THERON: The attorney, Krog, informed the forensic auditors firm who conducted the forensic analysis that they have determined during their interviews that the Financial Services Board (FSB) investigated LLL during may 2017 and referred the matter to the south African Reserve Bank. The FSB issued a notification that AW Theron is not registered as a financial services provider in terms of the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN LLL AND INVESTORS: According to the MOU signed between the LLL and investors: "Funds will be placed in an accredited online trading account, and trading will take place on an accredited trading platform, of which account trader (A'riel Willem Theron [ID: 880917 5149 083]) and EA's (Expert Advisors) will be the predominant trading tools, trading a variety of Forex currencies. The agreement is that all deposited funds will grow at a monthly rate of 8%, cumulative." LLL'S BANK ACCOUNTS FROZEN AND CLOSED: "One company that appeared to have been a forex trader was identified "FNB froze LLL's accounts in mid 2017 "During the latter part of 2017, FNB closed LLL's bank accounts "Krog explained that two employees then agreed to set-up a company called Lemon Tree Admin (Pty) Ltd - They opened a Standard Bank account in the name if Lemon Tree. LLL transferred funds to Lemon Tree's account to mostly make further payments to investors AW THERON'S EXPLANATION AS TO WHAT HAPPENED TO MONEY: The liquidator stated that when investors brought the liquidation application in December 2017, Theron responded that: "THE FUNDS WERE INVESTED IN BITCOIN BUT THEN STOLEN BY HACKERS". Moreover, "THAT ALL THE FUNDS ARE GONE". THERON LEAVING SA: Krog confirmed that AW Theron left South Africa for Brazil on 17 January 2018. The Ermelo Magistrate's Court issues a warrant for his arrest after investors in Ermelo laif a complaint with the SAPS. THERON ALLEGEDLY FALSIFIED LLL'S AVATRADER ACCOUNT AND BALANCE INFORMATION: "From information provided by Krog, it seems that AW Theron showed protential investors an AvaTrader account statement that indicated the balance as USD110 923 462.90 (110 million US dollars) on 31 December 2017. "In an email, on 19 March 2018 mr Ian Webb from AvaTrader, however, stated that: "I can confirm that the attached is not a true document. It is a screenshot from Ava Metatrader login page but the details have been altered." "The correct balance was confirmed to be USD353 Extra Budget Items: 1. Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 20 November 2018 Press Release: Ermelo Investment Horror It’s been ten months since the R290 million crypto-currency investment scheme Love and Let’s Live initially operating from Ermelo, Mpumalanga, collapsed, leaving more than 1300 investors, including pensioners and local business owners in a deep financial crisis. Trading on neighbourly trust and lifetime acquaintances, the company owner promised investors 8% monthly returns which were initially promptly paid out, attracting even more investors. Now the forex trader has fled the country. Carte Blanche uncovers how the scheme collapsed – leaving hundreds of devastated investors behind. Producer: Esté de Klerk Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli Script: ERMELO PONZI SCHEME PRODUCER: ESTE DE KLERK PRESENTER: MACFARLANE MOLELI EDITOR: STENETTE GROSKOPF BROADCAST DATE: 11 NOVEMBER 2018 When Meyerton resident William Holliday's father, Alfred passed away in November 2016, he had only one wish: that 34-year old William should take care of his stepmom, Phoebe and his two younger brothers. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Hy het my aanhoudend gevra, veral die laaste rukkie, "Asseblief kyk na jou broers. Kyk na die geld. Maak seker dit is vasbelê. (He asked me continuously, especially towards the end, "Please look after your brothers. Look after the money. Make sure that it's invested.") Financially, William's dad provided well for the family and it was only a matter of where to invest the money to secure their future. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Ons het 'n belegging gesoek om 'n manier om die geldjies te bele sodat ons kan vir die kinders se kollege, as hulle kollege wil gaan - eerste karretjie, sulke goedjies. (We were looking for an investment, a way to invest the money for the children's future college education, would they want to go to college… for their first cars, things like that.) A'ri'El Willem Theron immediately came to mind. William met Theron years ago and remembered him speaking about his business - investing people's money with above average return on investments. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Hy was redelik baie wetend, baie intelligent, so ek het nogal geglo hy maak die geld. Ek het nogal geval vir dit. (He was relatively knowledgeable, very intelligent… So, I believed he made the money. I fell for it.) PHOEBE HOLLIDAY: So het ek my geld toe in Januarie 2017 daar bele. En ek dink my eerste payout wat ek gekry het was in Maart. Ek het vir die kinders gesê daardie jaar ek gaan sabbatical vat. (So, I invested my money there in January 2017. And I think I received my first pay-out in March. I told the children that I was going to take a sabbatical that year.) Thirty-year old Willem Theron, originally from Ermelo in Mpumalanga, was described by many as a financial whizz kid - trading in a variety of foreign currency. Through his company - Love and Let's Live - he changed the financial prospects of his investors: an 8% monthly growth on investments. LINK: About 600 people from the town of Ermelo invested their money in Love and Let's Live and the town was abuzz with the new found wealth. However, it all came crashing down in January 2018. In just two years, more than 1300 people invested R290 million. The Love and Let's Live business model was based on what the South African Reserve Bank describes as a typical pyramid scheme: as long as new investors poured in money, the agreed 8% return on investment could be paid out to earlier-stage investors. HANNES MULLER: There was, however, no underlying business or trading. Liquidator, Hanner Muller - who handled Love and Let's Live's liquidation after the scheme collapsed - says forensic statements show that, contrary to Willem's written agreement with investors, only a fraction of the money was in fact traded in foreign currency. HANNES MULLER: only about five percent of what he ever collected was used for trading and that was done at a loss. Mathys Krog is an attorney assisting Hannes and his team in trying to recover some of the money. MATHYS KROG: He generated an Excel spreadsheet. People think, "I've invested R100 000. Now I've got R180 000 after three or four months." They will think that is the money they have in that account. Unfortunately, that was only a book entry. There was no such thing. Andre van Staden has been a restaurant owner in Ermelo for almost two decades. ANDRE VAN STADEN/RESTAURANT OWNER: If somebody comes to you in a community like this..." because we know everyone "... and shows you the papers and tell you, 'Andre, for the last 6 years I've been making R60,000 a month, I would believe them immediately. VO: Willem was a prefect at the Ermelo Christian School. LINK: Those who knew and grew up with him, described him as a humble, Christian boy who was loved and trusted by the community. ATHOL STARK: This was somebody that we knew. This was a personal family friend. Athol Stark is an astute businessman in Ermelo. He and two of his sons invested fairly large amounts. ATHOL STARK: What we definitely saw was that people's lifestyles had improved dramatically in the town. It was based on their success that other people started to jump on board. ANDRE VAN STADEN:People went to banks and borrowed money to put into this scheme. Many people took second mortgages on their homes. Ermelo residents were lining up - and like Theron's father, Andre - well-known in town - believed in the man who made it all happen. Andre Theron and his wife left town and moved to Makhado, but he agreed to speak to us telephonically. ANDRE THERON: He was trading successfully and that I still believe. It was never a big business from day one, it was just a small thing that grew. With Love and Let's Live offering a 2% "referral incentive ", friends informed friends and soon business was booming - for Willem Theron and his investors. ANDRE THERON: Willem never ever asked anybody to invest in his business, never. So, he got people asking him if they could invest and he always told them exactly that it is high risk, he is doing well. In April last year, R41 million flowed from Love and Let's Live's bank accounts as a cash deposit for the ultimate gift from son to father: a 3000 hectare luxury game and apple farm nestled in the lush green hills of the Mpumalanga highveld. The Therons had big plans, stocking the farm with valuable game and transforming an old shed to extravagant hunter's lodgings. Gerhard Serfontein was the building contractor. MACFARLANE MOLELI: What did it cost to build this place? GERHARD SERFONTEIN: It cost approximately 3 point something million. This was built especially for hunters coming from America and Spain and all over. Not only did Willem's dad profit. A forensic report indicates that R15,3 million was disbursed to Willem and his closest family members. More than R6 million was siphoned to Willem himself. MACFARLANE: Did you get up to R15 million, and your family, from your son, Willem? ANDRE THERON: I SPENT EVERYTHING ON THE FARM. The money was used for the farm, it went through my account, but I didn't use it for myself. According to the report, of the R290 million invested, R196 million was paid back to investors between 2015 and 2017. Theron, however, was trading illegally. MACFARLANE: Did he have an FSB licence? ANDRE THERON: No, of course what he did was illegal - and I know that he was trying to get it legalised. It seemed that Theron was caught off-guard when the Financial Services Board issued a warning to the public in July last year not to invest with Love and Let's Live as the company was not an authorised Financial Services Provider. Shortly after this, the bank froze the company accounts. Between August 2017 and January this year, Willem Theron wrote a series of letters to investors - promising full refunds to them all. PHOEBE HOLLIDAY: Daardie September toe my huur moes betaal toe is daar net nie die fondse nie. (That September, when I had to pay my rent, there were no funds available.) WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: My stiefma het goed uit haar huis begin verkoop om net vanaf te lewe. My stepmom started to sell things in her house in order to be able to survive. Willem Theron did not respond to our questions, but in a leaked telephone conversation with investors earlier this year, he explained he drained his international trading account worth over a hundred million dollars - and poured all the money into buying Bitcoin at 8000 dollars per unit. [MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: Die bitcoin wat ons gekoop het, was meer as 14 000 bitcoin. (The Bitcoin that we bought was more than 14 000 Bitcoin.) But the forensic auditors couldn't find any Bitcoin ledger transactions that proved this. MATHYS KROG: We did find a Bitcoin wallet. There were at one stage 213 or 217 Bitcoins.we traced about 157 of those Bitcoins. In correspondence to investors, Theron stated that Love and Let's Live was not a ponzi scheme. He insisted that he had more than double what was owed to clients and that the majority of the money in the international trading account was his. [MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: DIE Klientegeld wat in die rekening was was 50 million dollar en die res van die geld was myne. The clients' money that was in the account was 50 million dollar and the rest of the money was mine. In early January, he announced he was closing the business and all outstanding investments would be refunded. However, two weeks later, he claimed the Bitcoin he "had in storage for the remainder of the payments was stolen through a sophisticated and ruthless hacking operation". He fled the country and said he hoped investors would one day be able to forgive him. MACFARLANE: WHERE IS YOUR SON AT THE MOMENT? VOICE OF ANDRE THERON: HE IS SOMEWHERE IN SOUTH AMERICA MACFARLANE: Why did he run away, why isn't he coming to face the music? VOICE OF ANDRE THERON: The question is this: are you ready to ask your son to come back and let him go to a South African jail? [MARCH 2018] VOICE OF WILLEM THERON: Ek gaan nie lieg as ek se ek is nogsteeds baie dankbaar dat ek nie raakgesien word op hierdie oomblik nie, ek is baie skaam daaroor. Ek is ook baie jammer vir alles wat tot dusver gebeur het. (I'm not going to lie when I say I am still very thankful that I am not being seen at this moment - I feel very ashamed. I am also very sorry for what has happened thus far.) VOICE OF ANDRE VAN STADEN: When all the news came through, that 2 months were terrible for us because we could see people were spending less money. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Nie net dat ons almal gedependant aan die geld wat gaan uit gaan betaal word nie, so al die skuld wat ons gemaak het sou gecover gewees het. vir my ook omdat ek alles verloor het, maar meer vir my stiefma omdat dit my boeties se toekoms is. Not only were we all dependent on the money that was going to be paid out because all the debt we entered into would have been covered by that. The realisation that everything is gone, is a lot for me to handle. Obviously, also for myself because I have lost everything, but more so for my stepmom because it's my brothers' future… It would have secured her future. ATHOL STARK: "How could he do this to us?" This was somebody that we actually trusted. To make matters worse, every cent that investors RECEIVED in interest on their initial investments, they now have to pay back to the liquidators as stipulated by the Insolvency Act. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: Ek moet 120 duisend terug betaal. My stiefma moet 200 duisend terug betaal. Ons het nie daardie geld nie. I have to pay back R120 000. My stepmom has to pay back R200 000. We don't have that kind of money. The farm was liquidated and sold on auction and like so many other investors, Andre Theron says he also lost everything. ANDRE THERON: A LOT OF PEOPLE LOST EVERYTHING, I AM ONE OF THEM, I AM TRYING TO BUILD A NEW LIFE A total of eight fraud cases have been opened against Willem Theron and the police has issued a warrant for his arrest. To date, the liquidators have only been able to recover R7 million. Many investors will never see their money again. ATHOL STARK: Hundreds of people in this town are in severe financial crisis. They've lost their homes. They've lost their vehicles. They've lost their pensions based on what have happened with Willem Theron and his scheme. ****** PROMOS PROMO 1: 30" Would you invest money when someone you trust offers you a lifetime-opportunity to earn higher-than-bank returns? ANDRE VAN STADEN: People went to banks and borrowed money to put into this scheme. Many people took second mortgages on their homes. More than a thousand people invested R290 million in a scheme initially run from Ermelo, Mpumalanga and are reeling from shock after the scheme's collapse. WILLIAM HOLLIDAY: My stiefma het goed uit haar huis begin verkoop om net vanaf te lewe. PROMO 2: 15" A financial whizz kid from Ermelo in Mpumalanga dramatically changed the lives of more than a thousand people who invested millions with his company. But then the scheme collapsed and the whizz kid fled the country. ATHOL STARK: How could he do this to us, cause this is someone that we actually trusted? PROMO 3: 15" More than 600 residents of Ermelo in Mpumalanga invested millions with a local financial "whizz kid" they all trusted. ATHOL STARK: people's lifestyles had improved dramatically in the town. Until the scheme collapsed… and they lost everything. Residents in town now reeling with shock. Theron falsified a Forex Trading account statement which he showed to investors in December 2017, that stated there was USD110 million in the account, when in fact there was only USD353 in the account. The forensic audit states that only 1,5% of the total amount invested was in fact traded on foreign currencies and this was done at a loss. So what happened to all the money?
metadata.Summary: -An application to liquidate - or wind-up - Love and Let's Live Pty (Ltd), the company belonging to A'riel Willem Theron - a 30-year old resident from Ermelo who operated a so-called "Ponzi scheme" with 1 356 investors' money - was brought by creditors as an urgent application in the Pretoria High Court on 6 December 2017 -A provisional liquidation order was issued by the Pretoria High Court on 30 January 2018 -A Final liquidation order was issued on 16 March 2018 -The effective date of the liquidation of LLL was on 6 December 2017 - the date on which the urgent application was heard by the Pretoria High Court -On 6 February 2018, Hannes Muller and Lariska Arends from the Tshwane Trust in Pretoria were appointed as the provisional liquidators of LLL -Muller and Arends immediately started to act according to the insolvency legislation - seizing assets and financial records of LLL. They also approached the High Court to ask for permission to start formal and official questioning of related individuals -The liquidators don't know what the current whereabouts of Theron are - he earlier informed them via email that he is "now living a wanderer's lifestyle in South America", and he refused to provide the liquidators with any information to assist them with their investigation -The financial records were investigated and forensic report was written containing information about how money flowed in the company -1 357 Investors paid over a total amount of R290 390 780 to LLL -According to a written agreement between investors and LLL, a return in investment of between 72 and 96% would have been derived from trade in foreign currency -From the financial records, it seems that only 5,12% of investors' money LLL received was in fact used to trade in foreign currency AND these investments were traded against a loss
metadata.Further information: -The return in investment (monies) paid out to investors by far superseded the identifiable sources of income and the excessive returns paid out to certain investors were paid from funds received from other investors = Ponzi scheme -From the forensic report, it seems that LLL's liabilities exceeded its assets - possibly already as early as two months after LLL started to do business with investors -A further complication was that some investors didn't pay over their investment monies to the bank accounts of LLL, but to Theron's personal bank account and some specifically paid it over to a bank account Theron holds in Mauritius -The liquidators were able to determine that no money remained in the Mauritius account when LLL was liquidated - but they need to obtain a court order in Mauritius - a lengthy and costly exercise - in order to have access to bank statements of that account -An amount of at least R15 352 326 (R15 million) was siphoned from LLL's bank accounts to close family relatives of Theron, LLL director. A further amount of R8 million (R8 388 138) was given to Theron's sister with which she bought a property in Cape Town. The liquidators have already started the process to seize money and assets that were unlawfully siphoned to Theron's family members -R51-million (R51 743 200) of the money received by LLL was used to purchase a farm just outside Ermelo in the name of a company called "Ruby Success Inv - an entity of which Theron's father, Andre Theron was a director. The liquidators managed to have Ruby Success liquidated and Willem Theron sequestrated - declared insolvent -Provisional curators were appointed in the insolvent estate of Theron and they're currently in the process of selling the assets contained in the estate - two properties in Pretoria of which he is a 50% owner, furniture and three vehicles - it is not plausible that excessive funds would be obtained from selling his personal assets: the vehicles are still under financing and the properties still under mortgage. -The assets in Ruby Success - the farm - was sold on auction for R22-million (R22 200 000), so at a loss of R29-million of the price Theron paid when he bought it. -The liquidators have received claims from 450 creditors for a total amount of R170-million (R170 085 843,56). The liquidators are investigating the amounts claimed from creditors, as it seems that creditors have not only claimed the money they invested with LLL, but also the astronomical return on investment they were promised -According to Insolvency Legislation - also used in court cases such as the infamous Krion case - the aim is to fairly divide the return on assets amongst creditors - obtained from liquidated entities - the legislation makes provision that - for the time period before the entity was liquidated -- transactions that took place in favor of certain investors in comparison with other investors who were not advantaged - should be set aside = this means that the astronomical return in investments that investors received are now being seized to claim back money that would then later fairly be distributed between all the creditors -After the provisional liquidation date of LLL on 6 December 2017, LLL paid back certain investors' monies. According to article 341 (2) of the Companies' Act, such payments are regarded as null and void and those monies have to be seized by the liquidators -LLL also started to pay back investors' money shortly before the liquidation on 6 December - it seems that the aim was to pay back investors who'd put in less money, first at the expense of investors who invested large sums of money. The liquidators are also currently seizing any money paid back to investors within a six month period before LLL was liquidated (in terms of to Article 29 of the Insolvency Act). -According to the liquidators it is CLEAR that LLL was run as an illegal scheme and therefore all the exorbitant amounts of interest on their return on investments paid to investors, were done unlawfully and illegally. In terms of the Insolvency Act (article 26) all the interest received by investors have to be paid back as what is termed "disposals without value". -As soon as the liquidators have finished the process, the available funds would be divided on a pro rata base to creditors - this could still take months due to certain court actions that need to take place -Up until this stage, a total amount of R5,78 million (R5 798 616,23) has been seized by the liquidators. INFORMATION GATHERED FROM THE FORENSIC REPORT (NOT TO BE QUOTED DIRECTLY) DEFINITIONS OF A PONZI SCHEME: THE USA'S SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE COMMISSION DEFINITION: "A Ponzi scheme is an investment fraud that involves the payment of purported returns ro existing investors from funds contributed by new investors. Ponzi scheme organisers often solicit new investors by promising to invest funds in opportunities claimed to generate high returns with little or no risk. In many Ponzi schemes, the fraudsters focus on attracting new money to make promised payments to earlier-stage investors to create false appearance that investors are profiting from a legitimate business." THE SOUTH AFRICAN RESERVE BANK DEFINITION: "Names after the person - Charles Ponzi - who first made these schemes infamous, they are operated by tricksters and sometimes seemingly legitimate businesses that will invite you to invest in a scheme or business. The operator promises you unrealistically large returns on your investment in a short period of time. These schemes depend on enticing a steady flow of investors, whose money goes to pay off promises made to earlier investors. Any such scheme will inevitably collapse, as it is impossible to find enough investors to keep the scheme going." PONZI SCHEMES SHARE CERTAIN COMMON CHARACTERISTICS (A LAWYER MUST EXPLAIN THIS) "The purported business underlying the investment scheme depends on the inflow of external investor money; "The investor money is not used according to the stated business purpose. Instead, the investor money is used to pay returns to earlier investors, to often fund the perpetrator's lifestyle, or for some other illegitimate prupose; "The purported business enterprise underlying the scheme lacks sufficient profit to provide the returns and, therefore, depends on a continually increasing inflow of new investor money, and "Ponzi schemes often involve a charismatic and confident central promoter who successfully swindles investors SABRICS'S WARNING SIGNS OF A PONZI SCHEME: "The promoter promises high returns, which could not be achieved through normal conventional investment opportunities, within a short period. "In some cases, the promoter will use fake qualifications or references to entice investors, for example, an "attorney with many years' experience in the stock market" "Often high returns are paid initially, and then investors are lured into investing even more money "They often promise guaranteed returns - no return is ever guaranteed, all investments carry some risk "Promoters are usually quite secretive about the actual business model "The promoter becomes unavailable and returns dry up "Usually, the scheme collapses soon after that FSB ISSUED A WARNING ABOUT ADNRE WILLEM THERON: The attorney, Krog, informed the forensic auditors firm who conducted the forensic analysis that they have determined during their interviews that the Financial Services Board (FSB) investigated LLL during may 2017 and referred the matter to the south African Reserve Bank. The FSB issued a notification that AW Theron is not registered as a financial services provider in terms of the Financial Advisory and Intermediary Services Act 37 of 2002. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN LLL AND INVESTORS: According to the MOU signed between the LLL and investors: "Funds will be placed in an accredited online trading account, and trading will take place on an accredited trading platform, of which account trader (A'riel Willem Theron [ID: 880917 5149 083]) and EA's (Expert Advisors) will be the predominant trading tools, trading a variety of Forex currencies. The agreement is that all deposited funds will grow at a monthly rate of 8%, cumulative." LLL'S BANK ACCOUNTS FROZEN AND CLOSED: "One company that appeared to have been a forex trader was identified "FNB froze LLL's accounts in mid 2017 "During the latter part of 2017, FNB closed LLL's bank accounts "Krog explained that two employees then agreed to set-up a company called Lemon Tree Admin (Pty) Ltd - They opened a Standard Bank account in the name if Lemon Tree. LLL transferred funds to Lemon Tree's account to mostly make further payments to investors AW THERON'S EXPLANATION AS TO WHAT HAPPENED TO MONEY: The liquidator stated that when investors brought the liquidation application in December 2017, Theron responded that: "THE FUNDS WERE INVESTED IN BITCOIN BUT THEN STOLEN BY HACKERS". Moreover, "THAT ALL THE FUNDS ARE GONE". THERON LEAVING SA: Krog confirmed that AW Theron left South Africa for Brazil on 17 January 2018. The Ermelo Magistrate's Court issues a warrant for his arrest after investors in Ermelo laif a complaint with the SAPS. THERON ALLEGEDLY FALSIFIED LLL'S AVATRADER ACCOUNT AND BALANCE INFORMATION: "From information provided by Krog, it seems that AW Theron showed protential investors an AvaTrader account statement that indicated the balance as USD110 923 462.90 (110 million US dollars) on 31 December 2017. "In an email, on 19 March 2018 mr Ian Webb from AvaTrader, however, stated that: "I can confirm that the attached is not a true document. It is a screenshot from Ava Metatrader login page but the details have been altered." "The correct balance was confirmed to be USD353
